learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering
Ability to apply quality principles and methods
Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Structure discourse to facilitate the understanding of the objectives, actions, and/or results of one's own work.
Develop professional texts or scientific-technical reports according to the conventions of the discipline.
Adapt content organization and the use of verbal and non-verbal language to argue in various situations and/or before various audiences.
Solve complex problems autonomously within the discipline.
Effectively apply techniques related to bibliographic search and the use of reliable data sources or other information systems.

teaching_methods: Integrated project for problem solving (planning, design, realization)
Group work (preparation of essays, problem solving, projects)
Individual study (preparation of readings, exams, exercises, classes)
Classroom theory (lectures via slides, whiteboard, Teams)
Classroom practice (problem solving in class or via Teams using Florida Oberta)
Level tests (questionnaires, forms via Forms and/or Florida Oberta)
assessment_rules: The final grade requires a score of 5 or higher and a minimum of 4 in the written tests for each semester. Two written tests are conducted per semester, and an average of 4 out of 10 is required from these to combine with other parts. For students exempt from the integrated project, its weight is transferred to the written tests. In the second sitting, only written tests and the integrated project are considered, with written test grades of 4 or higher from the first or second semester being kept. Failure to meet both conditions results in a 'No Presentado' (Did Not Attend) or a maximum of 4 on the final grade if attending the exam.
